observations: Two large head-like shapes in profile sit side by side against a near-black background, both oriented toward the right, outlined in pale pink and lavender lines that trace jaw, crown, and chin edges.
Dense interior layers of purple, teal, yellow, red, and coral loops fill both forms, with repeated circular scribbles clustered where eye sockets and mouths would sit.
A coral-pink form projects from the left head into the gap between the two figures, its smooth curves contrasting with the tangled lines packed inside each shape.
reading: Two hollow-looking heads face the same direction, packed with overlapping color tangles that make their interiors feel restless and crowded. The coral projection from the left head—readable as a nose or jaw—reaches into the dark gap but does not bridge the two forms, leaving each figure isolated despite their closeness. The left head tilts slightly upward while the right juts forward and down, lending the pair an uneven, processional quality.
contextAngle: In the owned Scrimshaw subset, this work sits between Scrimshaw 24 and Scrimshaw 40 by title number. Both neighbors show single heads; the doubled composition here stands out. Across the collection, scrimshaw and nnxyz works share dense-line, dark-ground approaches to face-like forms.

connections.reason: Scrimshaw 24 fills a single head with similar purple and teal scribble density, but its lavender background and frontal stare contrast with the dark ground and paired profile format here.
Nifty faces #122 shares the black background and looping line clusters inside a rounded head form, but uses black outlines and a three-quarter view rather than colored-line profiles.

lookingQuestion: Both heads face the same way yet differ in tilt and posture—what visible details in their outlines or interior marks make one feel more assertive than the other?
ambiguities: Whether the coral form projecting from the left head is a nose, jaw extension, or separate element is visually ambiguous.
The comparison to nifty faces #122 rests on shared line-and-dark-ground qualities; the two artists' works differ in outline weight and spatial depth.
